content.text: The text is a sprawling nineteenth-century miscellany blending speculative science, poetry, myths, history, journalism, and travel narrative. It describes a fantastical Dudzeele deep-mine catastrophe ending in volcanic eruption; poems celebrate self-sacrifice, love, progress, liberty, marriage, and loss. “Whitherward” imagines humanity’s evolution from matter toward spiritual transformation. Other pieces recount myths of marriage and Odin’s nine-pins, compare George Washington with George III, and praise Masonry. Historical chapters discuss science, art, the Boers’ migration and wars, Johannesburg’s gold boom, the Jameson Raid, Boer society, President Kruger, and Cecil Rhodes. Explicit movements include Sandra moving to the hallway, Mary traveling to the office, the narrator descending Telegraph Hill and going home, and Kruger leaving his cottage for the Government Building.
